stem: A study records two binary results for each participant: whether an exposure is present and whether an outcome occurs. Each combination is possible. Which of the following sets is the sample space for one participant’s paired record?

options.label: A
options.text: Exposure present with outcome; exposure absent without outcome
options.explanation: This set contains the two matching combinations but omits the discordant combinations. A sample space must include every possible paired record, not only selected patterns.
options.misconception: Omits discordant exposure-outcome combinations from the possible outcomes.

options.label: B
options.text: Exposure and outcome; exposure only; outcome only; neither
options.explanation: There are four possible combinations of two binary results: both present, exposure alone, outcome alone and neither. This set includes every possible record described by the study.
options.misconception: No misconception: four joint combinations exhaust two binary observations.

options.label: C
options.text: Exposure present with outcome; exposure present without outcome
options.explanation: This set restricts attention to exposed participants and omits both possibilities for unexposed participants. It is a subset of the full sample space for one paired record.
options.misconception: Restricts the sample space to exposed participants.

options.label: D
options.text: Exposure absent with outcome; exposure absent without outcome
options.explanation: This set restricts attention to unexposed participants and omits both possibilities for exposed participants. The sample space must include all four combinations allowed by the study.
options.misconception: Restricts the sample space to unexposed participants.

options.label: E
options.text: Exposure present with outcome; exposure absent with outcome
options.explanation: This set restricts attention to participants with the outcome and omits those without it. The full sample space must also include both exposure states when the outcome is absent.
options.misconception: Omits both exposure states when the outcome is absent.

context:
Learning objective: Enumerate the sample space before assigning probabilities to joint exposure and outcome categories.

There are four possible combinations of two binary results: both present, exposure alone, outcome alone and neither. This set includes every possible record described by the study.
imageCaption: Null hypothesis, independence, and sample space on one board.
